Maritime NDT training in San Diego: the short answer

Short answer: Atlantis NDT trains San Diego ship-repair contractors, fabricators and technicians to ASNT SNT-TC-1A Level I, II and III in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET. Theory runs live online or onsite at your facility, practicals run on real specimens under an ASNT Level III, and your employer certifies you under its written practice. Navy repair contracts may add NAVSEA qualification, which the contractor's programme controls.

San Diego's maritime inspection market is shaped more by repair than by new construction. The Navy's Pacific surface fleet, aircraft carriers and submarines are homeported or maintained here, and the private yards and repair firms that service them run a constant cycle of availabilities, each with its own inspection scope, deadlines and audit trail. That rhythm rewards technicians who can move quickly between methods and employers who keep their certification files in order. This section explains how SNT-TC-1A training fits that market, where Navy-specific qualification takes over, and how to get training delivered without pulling a crew off a repair job for a week. There is no Atlantis classroom in San Diego or elsewhere in California; we deliver live online or at your shop.

If you already know what you need, request a San Diego maritime training quote. Cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day.

Maritime NDT work in San Diego Bay

General Dynamics NASSCO is the West Coast's largest new-construction shipyard, building auxiliary and support ships for the Navy alongside commercial vessels, and it also performs repair work. BAE Systems runs a major ship repair yard on the bay. Around them sits a large community of ship repair contractors, many working under the Navy's Master Ship Repair Agreement or Agreement for Boat Repair frameworks, together with the specialist subcontractors who do the welding, machining, coatings and inspection inside each availability.

Demand comes from several Navy installations: Naval Base San Diego on 32nd Street, the largest surface-ship base on the West Coast; Naval Air Station North Island on Coronado, where aircraft carriers are homeported; and Naval Base Point Loma, home to submarines. Federal maintenance organisations manage the repair work and set the technical requirements that flow down to contractors. The result is steady inspection volume in thickness surveys, weld repair acceptance, piping and valve work, and structural repairs on decks, foundations and hull plating.

The county's aerospace and energy manufacturers draw on the same technician pool. Gas turbine production, unmanned aircraft and defence electronics work bring PT, ET, UT and RT demand under aerospace specifications, which is useful to know if you are planning a career that may cross from the waterfront to a manufacturing floor.

Which NDT methods San Diego maritime work uses, and under which rules

This table is context for planning training. The contract, the work item and the purchase order always define the code, edition and acceptance clause.

MethodMaritime application in San DiegoCode or standard usually cited
UT (Level I, II, III)Thickness surveys on hull, tank and piping during availabilities; shear-wave examination of repair weldsMIL-STD-2035 for naval acceptance; ABS rules for commercial; ASME V
PAUTEncoded weld examination and corrosion mapping where permitted by the contractContract technical requirements; ASME V Article 4
TOFDFlaw sizing on thick welds in new construction and commercial repairASME V; customer specification
RTPiping and pressure-boundary welds requiring a permanent imageMIL-STD-2035; ASME V; B31.1 or B31.3 piping codes
MTCrack detection on steel repair welds, back-gouges and structural membersMIL-STD-2035; AWS D1.1; ASME V Article 7
PTAluminium superstructures and fittings, stainless and copper-nickel piping, non-magnetic valve bodiesMIL-STD-2035; ASME V Article 6
VTVisual acceptance of every repair weld and fit-up; first method in any jobMIL-STD-2035 visual criteria; AWS D1.1
ETHeat-exchanger and condenser tubing; surface checks on non-ferrous partsCustomer specification

Method spotlight: PT and UT thickness. Aluminium content in modern ships and the volume of copper-nickel and stainless piping keep PT unusually busy in San Diego, and almost every availability starts with UT thickness surveys to define the repair scope. A technician with solid PT and UT thickness skills at Level II is useful from the first week of an availability.

Which certification scheme San Diego maritime employers expect

Atlantis trains to ASNT SNT-TC-1A. The rest of this table describes what employers may require on top, not something we provide.

SchemeWho in San Diego requires itDoes SNT-TC-1A training fit?
ASNT SNT-TC-1A (employer-based)Commercial repair yards, fabricators, inspection firms, many subcontractorsYes. This is what we train to, and your employer certifies you under its written practice.
NAVSEA T9074-AS-GIB-010/271Contractors performing NDT on Navy ship work where the contract invokes itAs a foundation. Naval qualification and certification run through the contractor's NAVSEA-compliant programme; a commercial course does not grant it.
Naval nuclear and submarine-specific requirementsWork on submarines and nuclear-powered carriers' controlled systemsNo. These are programme-controlled qualifications.
Class society expectations (ABS and others)Commercial vessels repaired or built under classUsually yes, subject to the yard's approved procedures and surveyor acceptance.
NAS 410 / EN 4179Aerospace manufacturers in the countyPartly. Aerospace employers certify under their own NAS 410 written practice with a responsible Level 3. SNT-TC-1A theory is a foundation; we do not offer NAS 410 certification.

The practical takeaway for a San Diego technician: an employer-certified SNT-TC-1A Level II in VT, MT, PT and UT is the most portable credential on the waterfront, and your Navy-contract employer will layer NAVSEA qualification over it where the work requires.

The SNT-TC-1A certification path for San Diego technicians, step by step

  1. Your employer's written practice. Each employer writes its own procedure setting training, experience, exams and certification authority. See written practice development if yours needs one.
  2. Formal training. Theory in the method and level. Recommended minimum hours are listed in our training requirements matrix; the written practice sets the actual figure.
  3. On-the-job experience. Logged, supervised time on real work. Repair availabilities generate plenty of it; the challenge is documenting it properly.
  4. Examinations. General, specific and practical exams administered and graded by a Level III, with the practical on real specimens.
  5. Vision examination. Near-vision and colour contrast checks on the written practice's schedule.
  6. Employer certification. Signed by your employer and valid under that written practice.
  7. Recertification. At the interval your written practice defines.

For the whole scheme, see SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Radiation licensing and port access for San Diego RT crews

California is an NRC Agreement State, and the California Department of Public Health's Radiologic Health Branch licenses radioactive materials and registers X-ray equipment. California also issues its own industrial radiographer certificates under Title 17 of the California Code of Regulations, so a radiographer working in the state needs the CDPH certification in addition to the employer's NDT certification. An RT method course from any provider does not by itself satisfy the state requirement. Your company's radiation safety officer will specify what is needed.

Access is the other practical hurdle. Navy installations require base access credentials arranged through the employer, and commercial marine terminals regulated under the Maritime Transportation Security Act require a TWIC for unescorted access. If you want onsite training inside a controlled area, raise it at quote stage; it is often simpler to run the practical block at your own shop.

How San Diego crews can take the training

  • Live online theory. Instructor-led sessions on Pacific time with recorded review, scheduled around shifts. See NDT training online.
  • Onsite at your facility. A Level III runs the course at your shop with your equipment and procedures. Ideal between availabilities, and the best preparation for a prime-contractor or Navy audit because the training uses the procedures the auditor will review.
  • Scheduled cohorts. Block courses quoted per cohort. We do not run a training centre in California.

Repair contractors live by the availability schedule, so we book onsite training into the gaps between jobs. Ask about onsite training for your San Diego crew and send us your quiet windows.

A training plan for a San Diego repair contractor

Repair contractors rarely need every method at once. A plan that fits the way availabilities actually run usually looks like this. Start with VT for every welder-inspector and QA hand, because visual acceptance comes first on every repair weld and a shortage of qualified VT people slows an entire job. Add MT and PT next, matched to the materials in your normal scope: steel structures and foundations for MT, aluminium, stainless and copper-nickel for PT. Then build UT in two stages, thickness gauging first because it drives scope definition at the start of each availability, then shear-wave weld examination for repair acceptance. PAUT and TOFD come last and only for the technicians who will use them, since they demand more experience and the contract has to permit them.

Spreading that plan across a year, in short onsite blocks between availabilities and live online theory in the evenings, keeps the crew working while it upgrades. It also produces a steady stream of documented training and experience hours, which is what your Level III needs to certify people without delay when a new contract arrives.

What a San Diego employer receives from an onsite course

Each technician leaves with a training record listing method, level, hours, dates, course outline and instructor; graded exam records where Atlantis administers exams under your written practice; a description of the practical specimens; and a short note on any gaps between your procedures and the work items or codes you inspect to. The records are designed to drop straight into certification files so that your Level III can sign certifications and an auditor can trace every hour.

Level III services and written practices for San Diego repair contractors

Small and mid-size repair subcontractors often discover during a contract award or audit that their NDT programme has gaps: a written practice copied from another firm, missing practical exam documentation, lapsed vision tests, or procedures that do not match the work item. We provide written practice development, procedure review, exam administration and ongoing Level III support, and multi-method programmes through corporate NDT training and maritime corporate training. Local consulting is described on maritime NDT consulting in San Diego, and Level III exam preparation is covered on ASNT Level III training in San Diego. Book a Level III consultation if your programme needs a review.

Practise before the practical exam

The Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees practise 12 methods in five environments, including a welding workshop, an NDT lab and a storage tank. It builds familiarity with set-up and scanning between theory sessions. It is practice only and never replaces the practical exam on real specimens.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who sets course content, administers and grades examinations where your written practice assigns that role to Atlantis, and reviews employer written practices.

Local NDT training options compared

  • Employer and shipyard programmes. The large yards and Navy-contract firms train and qualify their own inspection staff under naval requirements. For a career inside those programmes, apply directly.
  • Southern California NDT schools. Private schools in the Los Angeles and Orange County area run fixed-date classroom courses, and some Los Angeles programmes focus on aerospace NDT. They suit individuals who can commute or travel for a block course.
  • National online providers. Several schools sell self-paced online theory. Check whether your employer's written practice accepts self-paced hours before buying.
  • Atlantis NDT. Best for repair contractors, fabricators and inspection firms that want instructor-led SNT-TC-1A training live online or onsite with Level III and written-practice support.

See also NDT training in San Diego, the state hub NDT training in California, NDT training in Los Angeles, the national maritime NDT training page and aerospace NDT training. Other shipbuilding markets: Norfolk, Groton and Pascagoula.

Frequently asked questions about maritime NDT training in San Diego

How do I get NDT certified in San Diego?

Work for or be sponsored by an employer with an SNT-TC-1A written practice, complete formal training and logged experience, pass the general, specific and practical exams under a Level III, and pass the vision test. Your employer signs the certification.

Can I take NDT training online in California?

Yes, for theory. Practical training and exams are performed on real specimens, onsite at your employer or in a scheduled block.

Does Atlantis provide NAVSEA certification for ship repair?

No. NAVSEA qualification is administered within the contractor's NAVSEA-compliant programme. Our SNT-TC-1A training is the foundation many contractors build it on.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on your employer's written practice and your existing experience. Recommended minimums are in our training requirements matrix. Logged experience usually takes longer than the classroom part.

Do I need a licence for radiography in California?

Yes. California requires industrial radiographers to hold a state-issued certificate from CDPH under Title 17, and the company must hold a licence or registration for its sources or X-ray equipment.

What does maritime NDT training cost in San Diego?

Quote on request. Cost depends on method, level, number of trainees, online or onsite delivery and any Level III services. Request a quote and we reply within one business day.

Is ASNT certification recognised by San Diego ship repair employers?

Yes for commercial and most subcontract scope. Navy contracts that invoke NAVSEA requirements add their own qualification on top.

Can I use the GI Bill or WIOA funding?

Only at approved schools and programmes, and Atlantis does not claim that approval. San Diego has many transitioning service members; check with the VA, your base transition office or a local America's Job Center of California. Employer-paid training is the more common route in NDT. See veterans transitioning into NDT.

I was a Navy hull technician. Does that experience count?

Possibly toward on-the-job experience if it is documented and your new employer's written practice accepts it. Bring records of any inspection work you performed.

Which NDT method is most in demand on the San Diego waterfront?

UT thickness and VT start almost every repair job, with MT and PT close behind. Building all four to Level II gives you the widest options.

Is there an NDT training centre in San Diego?

Atlantis does not operate one. We deliver live online and onsite at employer facilities.

How do I prepare for the written exams?

Review your employer's procedures and use mock questions such as our UT Level 2 practice questions.
